description: The house's north (front) wall, wood-shingled, behind the open front porch that runs its whole width under the main roof; corner to corner (the corners are behind the porch's two end piers), from grade to the eave (the roof edge, 9'-5 1/4" above the first floor); two wide windows (four-light upper sashes) and the front door between them, all with their heads at the frieze band's bottom.

length.note: no string of its own on the plan (the left-side strings are the porch's): taken equal to the opposite (south) wall's printed 26'-2 1/2", as the house truth does. On the elevation the drawn outline is the porch's end piers' outer edges, x 8741 to 11337 px = 25.96 ft (the plan's porch string 1'-5 1/2" 7'-3" 1'-5 1/2" 5'-7 3/4" 1'-5 1/2" 7'-3" 1'-5 1/2" = 25.98 ft); the wall's own corners are hidden behind those piers.

eave.note: this elevation's printed levels: EAVE 9'-5 1/4" above the first floor (0'-0") plus the mean of its two printed grades, 4'-0" (left) and 3'-9 1/2" (right) below the floor = 9.4375 + 3.8958 = 13.333 ft. The house truth's heights.eave is 13.586 ft (the same eave level over the mean of all eight printed grades, 4.148 ft); the lot slopes, so this wall's grade is used here. The sheet is drawn about 0.65 deg off level (the floor leaders are at y 3130 px at x 8075 and 3081 px at x 12450; the frieze and the porch rail tilt the same way), so sill_ft is taken from the floor datum line, not from the drawn grade line (which lies 0.2 to 0.45 ft below the printed grades).

openings.note: mean of the passes. A: window schedule type 1 (plan sheet 3; schedule: sash C 3'-7 3/8" wide, B 5'-0 5/8" frame height, A 2'-6 5/8" upper sash; plan opening 3'-8 1/4"). Top is the frieze band's bottom, where the casings stop (the 7'-0 1/4" FASCIA level). The bottom is hidden by the porch's solid rail (its cap at y 2957.5 px): the box stops there; from B and the typical window's sill the trim probably reaches 0 to 0.25 ft lower. Right casing ends against the porch pier (x 9597, pier from 9606). | B: wide window (four-light upper sash) behind the porch; its right casing abuts a porch post (9610-9690), which may hide its last few px. The bottom is cut by the top of the porch's knee wall (2955): the sill is hidden. On the east elevation the windows' sills are about 1.5 ft above the floor (about y 2930 here), so the hidden part is probably small, but it was not read. The sheet's window schedule (types 1-10, frame sizes) is not keyed to this elevation, so it was not used.

mean of the passes. A: front door: casings x 9867 to 10224.5 px, top at the frieze bottom. Below y 2950 px it is hidden by the porch's solid rail; the bottom is the threshold at the printed FLOOR 0'-0" level (y 3108 px on the floor datum line at the door), so the height 6.97 ft equals the printed 7'-0 1/4" FASCIA level within 0.05 ft. The front door detail (sheet 6, 1" = 1'-0", 399 px/ft on its bar) scales 3.69 ft between the casings' outer edges and 6.96 ft from the head to the threshold line (7.28 ft to the porch floor line below it). | B: front door (four-light upper panel) behind the porch; its lower part is hidden by the porch knee wall, so the bottom is the floor line (the floor mark, 3079.5) per the threshold rule. The sheet 6 FRONT DOOR detail at 1" = 1'-0" (399.8 px/ft) scales 3.70 ft wide over the casings and about 6.98-7.1 ft from the head casing's top to the threshold, i.e. 0.26-0.4 ft taller than this box: the elevation's floor mark may sit about 0.3 ft high.

mean of the passes. A: window schedule type 1 (as W1). Top is the frieze band's bottom; bottom hidden by the porch's solid rail (cap at y 2941.5 px), the box stops there (probably 0 to 0.25 ft short). Left casing abuts the porch pier (pier to x 10486). | B: wide window (four-light upper sash) behind the porch; its left edge (10478) is where a porch post (10300-10480) ends, so its left casing may be partly hidden (it scales 0.23 ft wider than W1). Bottom cut by the porch knee wall's top (2941); the sill is hidden, as for W1.

porch: An open porch under the main roof runs the wall's whole width (about 9'-2 3/4" deep, 26'-6 1/4" long): four boxed piers stand in front of the wall (at both corners and either side of the door) and a solid shingled rail about 2 ft high hides the wall's lower part, the windows' sills and the door's bottom.
